Thesis
The book does three things no movie can
Not because the film is bad. It's wonderful.
I
A mind to inhabit
It takes you inside a character's head.
II
Time
It takes as long as the story needs.
III
A world you build
You imagine it yourself.
The Movie Plays in Your Head First
03 / 12
Point I
Inside Harry's mind
We don't just watch Harry. We are Harry.
On screen
An actor's face and a piece of music. Beautiful.
On the page
Pages inside his head: his longing, his confusion, his fear of losing it.
You live inside:
The cupboard under the stairs
The Mirror of Erised
The Movie Plays in Your Head First
04 / 12
Film is a window.
A book is a door.
One lets you look. The other lets you walk through.
Point II
Time creates depth
The film
152
minutes
About two and a half hours. Every scene has to earn its seconds.
The book
309
pages
As long as it needs. Room for side characters, jokes and quiet moments.

06 / 12
Point II · Lost in adaptation
Characters become shortcuts
Peeves
The poltergeist. Gone.
Hermione
On screen: “the smart one.”
Neville
On screen: “the clumsy one.”
Cut from film
In the book, they have room to be human.
The Movie Plays in Your Head First
07 / 12
Point III
You are the director
The film gave us one Great Hall. What does yours look like?
When you read, you are the…
Casting director
You choose every face.
Set designer
You build every room.
Cinematographer
You frame every shot.
The movie gave us one Hogwarts. The book gave each of us our own.
The Movie Plays in Your Head First
08 / 12
To be fair
What the film does best
The music
John Williams' score gives you chills before anyone says a word.
The casting
Hagrid will always be Robbie Coltrane.
The motion
Quidditch at full speed is thrilling.
The film adds to the story. It doesn't replace it.
The Movie Plays in Your Head First
09 / 12
The verdict
So, which is better?
The book.
Not because the movie is weak, but because the book gives you:
A mind to inhabit
Time to fall in love
A world that belongs to you
The Movie Plays in Your Head First
10 / 12
My challenge to you
Next time you're excited about an adaptation
STEP 1
Read the book first.
STEP 2
Let the movie play in your head.
STEP 3
Then see how someone else imagined it.

The best story isn't the one you watch.
It's the one you live in.
